content: 1. Laxminarayan R, Matsoso P, Pant S, Brower C, Røttingen JA, Klugman K, et al. discussed the global challenge of ensuring access to effective antimicrobials. This study, published in The Lancet in 2016 (Volume 387, Issue 10014, Pages 167-175), highlights the critical need for equitable access to these life-saving medications worldwide. 2. Pittet D, Sax H, Hugonnet S, and Harbarth S examined the financial implications of promoting successful hand hygiene practices. Their findings, published in Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology in 2004 (Volume 25, Issue 3, Pages 264-266), underscore the cost-effectiveness of hand hygiene interventions in healthcare settings. 3. Storr J, Twyman A, Zingg W, Damani N, Kilpatrick C, Reilly J, et al. provided evidence-based recommendations for the core components of effective infection prevention and control programs. This work, published in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2017 (Volume 6, Article 6), reflects new guidelines from the World Health Organization (WHO). 4. Kilpatrick CSJ, Zayed B, and Allegranzi B proposed a preliminary conceptual model exploring the relationship between two implementation approaches for preventing surgical site infections. Their study appeared in Antimicrobial Resistance and Infection Control in 2017 (Volume 6, Supplement 3, Abstract O48). 5. Carayon P, Xie A, and Kianfar S investigated the role of human factors and ergonomics as a patient safety practice. Their research, published in BMJ Quality & Safety in 2014 (Volume 23, Pages 196-205), emphasizes the importance of designing systems that enhance safety and reduce errors in healthcare. 6. Wick EC, Hobson DB, Bennett JL, Demski R, Maragakis L, Gearhart SL, et al. described the implementation of a comprehensive, unit-based safety program aimed at reducing surgical site infections. Their findings, published in Journal of the American College of Surgeons in 2012 (Volume 215, Pages 193-200), demonstrate the effectiveness of structured safety interventions in surgical settings.
